backlog.spec: Modify the optimization loop to expand the parameter update for matrix weights by adding a secondary updatable bias vector per layer, initialized small and updated via Adam. This soft expands the parameter space without increasing memory significantly if zeroed out when not needed.
backlog.title: Upd-Bias Expansion

backlog.spec: Alter the Adam update rule so that the momentum vector 'm' for weights is updated by subtracting a fraction of the global parameter 'p', i.e., m_new豪杰 = beta * m_old - alpha * p. This enforces a dependency on the prior global state, potentially smoothing gradients better in deep towers.
backlog.title: W-=P Momentum

backlog.spec: Replace the WARMUP_RATIO of 0.0 with a small positive value (e.g., 0.1) and change WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.0, and introduce a custom schedule where LR creeps down very slowly, then drops sharply near the end, keeping early training very stable.
backlog.title: Layer-Sequence Decay

backlog.spec: Split TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE into two halves per device: BatchA and BatchB. Train BatchA with normal dynamics, then switch weights to mimic a different data distribution for BatchB within the same step, or use two separate small batches to run a mixture step.
backlog.title: Halo-Batch Splitting

backlog.spec: Only add a tiny epsilon term to the weight update rule to increment weights by a constant factor (even if that factor is 0.0001), ensuring that even as the Adam terms decayed out, there is a baseline push.
backlog.title: Zeroed-Increment Update

backlog.spec: Modify the Adam optimizer application to apply updates only to scalar parameters (SCALAR_LR) and and EMBEDDING_LR) but use a very different learning rate for matrices. Use this to isolate embedding vs matrix tuning.
backlog.title: Scalar-Only Adam

backlog.spec: Introduce a time-dependent residual connection within the training loop: at global step t, add/explicitly an adapter layer to all hidden states that decays with t. This forces the model to evolve its behavior as it trains, rather than just static updates.
backlog.title: Time-Decay Adapters

backlog.spec: In the training loop, operate in two stages per optimizer step: one stage where ALL B64 token positions are updated normally, the next stage where we randomly drop 32% of tokens and recompute gradients for only the remaining ones.
backlog.title: Latent-Batch Swap

backlog.spec: Modify the output layer (lm_head) to perform a partial gradient update where updates are only applied to positions with an even index, then swap focus to odd indices in subsequent steps.
backlog.title: Positional-Sparse Update

backlog.spec: Reduce HEAD_DIM from 128 to 32 as a temporary change, forcing the model to learn fewer and more accurate features per attention head, then restore it later or use a dynamic final weight
backlog.title: Head-Dimension Downscaling

backlog.spec: Freeze all layers except the last two for the first 15s of the 300s window, then gradually unfreeze starting from the last layer upwards. This lets the model stabilize the top behavior before bottom optimization.
backlog.title: Depth-Freezing Warmup

backlog.spec: Set ALL Adam momentum 'm' vectors to zero for embedding and lm_head parameters, forcing them to rely solely on raw gradients without accumulated momentum.
backlog.title: Embedding-Only Momentum

backlog.spec: Replace the 'SSSL' window pattern with 'SSSSL' or 'L' (full context) windows, allowing the model to process a larger receptive field per step and thus have a more expressive evaluation capability.
backlog.title: Window-Expansion

backlog.spec: Change DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE to 32 and split the training workload so that each step processes two batches of size 32 instead of one batch of 64. This increases the total VRAM load but can be amortized trivially.
backlog.title: Batch-Size Fold

backlog.spec: After the standard Adam step, take the old weight and subtract a fraction of it (e.g., 0.1) from the new weights, before applying the next update. This introduces a slight 'forgetting' bias.
backlog.title: Grad-Cancel Update

backlog.spec: Lower UNEMBEDDING_LR from 0.004 to 0.0001, making its updates so slow that it barely affects the loss for most of the 300s window, allowing matrix weights to dominate the optimization.
backlog.title: Embedding-Decay Rate

backlog.spec: Add a new tiny bias vector injected into the hidden states of each transformer layer, updated independently via Adam. This effectively expands the capacity for non-linearities.
backlog.title: Hidden-Bias Injection

backlog.spec: Round the global step number at each optimizer step, ensuring that every N steps updates occur with the same multiplier. This forces progress to occur in discrete 'waves' rather than continuous flow.
backlog.title: Round-Step Update

backlog.spec: Run the Adam optimizer update only on the device where weights are stored (CUDA) and discard any intermediate partial sum logic that might be used for mixed-device training.
backlog.title: Device-Only Adam

backlog.spec: Reduce ASPECT_RATIO from 64 to 32, which halves model_dim and reduces memory by 50%, allowing for much higher effective batch size if you double device batch size
backlog.title: Seq-Length Reduction

backlog.spec: Start with a very high initial LR (e.g., 0.05 for MATRIX_LR) that decays linearly, then warm down aggressively over the remaining time. This lets the model learn fast features early.
backlog.title: LR-Spike Warmup

backlog.spec: In the training loop, after computing gradients, randomly shuffle the order in which layers are updated and applied. This introduces noise that may help escape local minima.
backlog.title: Local-Weight Shuffle

backlog.spec: For every other layer, set their recurrence weight to zero (or a small epsilon) for parts of the loop, effectively freezing them and only updating every second layer.
backlog.title: Semi-Frozen Layers

backlog.spec: Replace the static WINDOW_PATTERN with a dynamic pattern that adjusts based on the current position in the data sequence. Compute a variable window size per token.
backlog.title: Dynamic-Window Size

backlog.spec: Apply warmup to embedding and lm_head only, while keeping matrix parameters at full learned rate from the start. This prioritizes early embedding alignment.
backlog.title: Embed-Only Warmup

backlog.spec: In the training loop, before processing the full batch, inject a small amount of random 'noise' tokens (dummy vocab) into the input stream. This扰s the data slightly and forces the model to become more robust.
backlog.title: Data-Blend Injection

backlog.spec: Use a smaller cache size (or lower-depth cache) by reducing the days that you keep, potentially forcing the model to recompute certain operations more often.
backlog.title: Cache-Update Strategy

backlog.spec: Instead of applying the standard Adam update, accumulate the gradient sum over a window of steps (e.g., 10 steps) and apply a single averaged update at the end of that window.
backlog.title: Gradient-Cum-Sum

backlog.spec: Track the sum of squared gradients modulo the sequence length and apply a small penalty loss to prevent models from overfitting to short dependencies, which can lower val_bpb on longer sequences.
backlog.title: Gradient-Memory Pressure

backlog.spec: Switch to mixed precision (BF16/FP32) for optimizer states in AdamW to reduce memory fragmentation and allow slightly larger effective batches or faster convergence.
backlog.title: Mixed-Precision AdamW

backlog.spec: Preset the warmup fraction to zero but make the effective warmup duration depend on the total number of training steps and the current epoch to better match the optimization landscape.
backlog.title: Adaptive Warmup Steps

backlog.spec: Define a second training epoch at the tail end of the 300s budget, freezing dimensions except for specific tokens and layers to refine the final model without destabilizing the optimization.
backlog.title: Fine-Tuning Epochs

backlog.spec: Replace only 0.5% of tokens in the training loop with random tokens instead of 2%, reducing the noise impact while still providing a semblance of regularization.
backlog.title: Sparse Token Replacement

backlog.spec: Optionally add a small loss term for token positions that are not used in the loss calculation to improve the alignment between data distribution and token usage.
backlog.title: Token-Loss Balance

backlog.spec: Add a bias feed to the optimizer to ensure that the bias terms are updated at every step, improving the stability of the Adam optimizer.
backlog.title: Update Bias Feed

backlog.spec: Use a geometric window growth rate that is slightly different from the previous run to see if a subtle change in the sequence length distribution affects val_bpb.
backlog.title: Window-Growth Rate

backlog.spec: Halve the device batch size and increase the number of devices in a multi-GPU setting (if applicable) or keep it on a single device but increase the number of micro-batches to smooth the gradient.
backlog.title: Batch-Size Halving

backlog.spec: Apply a gradient accumulator decay factor to the gradients before the optimizer update to smooth out fluctuations in the gradient magnitude.
backlog.title: Gradient-Accumulator Decay

backlog.spec: Replace WINDOW_PATTERN = "SSSL" (half context) with a single layer setting to "LLLL" (full context) to allow full attention across the sequence length, provided the 40GB budget permits.
backlog.title: Window-Size Quadrupling (Architecture)

backlog.spec: Run with DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE = 4 to split the optimizer step into 16 smaller chunks per physical step, potentially bypassing KV cache bottlenecks at high sequence lengths.
backlog.title: Batch-Fragmentation (Batch)

backlog.spec: Increase WEIGHT_DECAY from 0.2 to 0.8 to aggressively compress model dimensions, hoping to lower val_bpb through regularization against overfitting.
backlog.title: Weight-Decay Aggression (Optimizer)

backlog.spec: Shift the start of LR warmup from step 0 to step 20% of the total budget, allowing the model to learn initial attention weights before increasing step size.
backlog.title: Warmup-Epoch Delay (Schedule)

backlog.spec: Reduce HEAD_DIM from 128 to 64 effectively reducing the model capacity per layer, forcing deeper layers and potentially lowering inference bits.
backlog.title: Channel-Dropout (Batch)

backlog.spec: Lower the gradient clipping norm from default (usually 1.0) to 0.1 to dampen large updates and reduce variance in later layers.
backlog.title: Gradient-Clip Magnitude (Optimizer)

backlog.spec: Hold the warmup rate to 0.0 for the first 500 epochs, allowing a stable initialization before applying the standard scheduling curve.
backlog.title: Layer-Merge Warmup (Schedule)

backlog.spec: Reduce ASPECT_RATIO from 64 to 32 and decrease HEAD_DIM proportionally to create a flatter model where fewer channels produce the same output.
backlog.title: Head-Per-Byte Scaling (Architecture)

backlog.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO = 0.3 and DANSE (direct, adaptive, non-standard schedule and early stopping) to 0.0 to apply a steeper initial learning rate boost.
backlog.title: AdamG Trend Peak (Optimizer)

backlog.spec: Remove the L2 normalization of embeddings at the start of training by commenting out that line, allowing embeddings to grow in magnitude with the data distribution.
backlog.title: Embedding-L2-Fix (Data)

backlog.spec: Increase HEAD_DIM from 128 to 256 and simultaneously increase DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE from 64 to 128. Since the model has 8 layers and the sequence length is constrained by the device VRAM (40GB), doubling the head dimension while doubling the batch size keeps the total trainable parameters roughly constant but effectively doubles the width per layer, allowing for a more robust feature space within the same memory footprint without increasing depth.
backlog.title: Wide-Head Bottleneck

backlog.spec: Introduce a dynamic affinity term to the Adam optimizer that decays the L2-norm of momentum vectors exponentially by a factor of 1.001 per step (equivalent to an exponential decay in the second moment of gradients), encouraging the optimizer to focus on persistent signal rather than canceling gradients. This is implemented by multiplying the exp_avg_sq term by exp(-1e-3) before the variance computation each step.
backlog.title: Exponential Variance Decay

backlog.spec: Instead of a linear warm-up that ramps up the learning rate to its maximum, implement a schedule where the learning rate is low initially, then increases sharply at a critical threshold (simulating the 'tunneling' through a barrier), and then decays over the remainder of training. This allows the model to start with high uncertainty and gradual recovery of precision later in the batch processing.
backlog.title: Quantum-Tunneling Warmup

backlog.spec: Add a layer-specific injection of noise where the first layer of each transformer block receives 10-15% of its input as random noise from the vocabulary. This forces the deepest layers to learn to denoise and aggregate information from the shallow layer, improving the efficiency of representation learning, especially given the shallow depth (8 layers).
backlog.title: Depth-Localized Input Perturbation

backlog.spec: Replace the standard cross-entropy or similar loss with a KL-divergence inspired loss that penalizes predictions that are too close to the mean distribution of the training data, effectively forcing the output to be sparse and distinct. This helps the model find clearer clusters in the latent space, improving generalization.
backlog.title: Kullback-Liebler Loss Amplification

backlog.spec: Modified attention heads to apply the attention mechanism across a fraction of the sequence length (e.g., only the first half of tokens) in parallel with the full-length attention on the second half, effectively creating a hierarchical attention mechanism that allows the model to coarse-grain before fine-graining without extra FLOPs due to the depth constraint.
backlog.title: Fractional-Layer Attention

backlog.spec: Divide the parameter groups by Adam into small sub-groups and compute momentum and variance for each sub-group independently, rather than aggregating them. This introduces a form of regularization that prevents the momentum vectors from dominating the updates, allowing for more stable convergence at high learning rates.
backlog.title: Grouped Adam Momentum

backlog.spec: Maintain a separate window for updates from small batch fragments (e.g., 12 tokens) versus full batch updates. After the full batch update is performed, blend the gradients from the fragment buffers into the main buffer, effectively using a continuous learning rate schedule that adapts to the varying magnitude of updates.
backlog.title: Scale-Invariant Batch Update

backlog.spec: Inject the full embedding vector into the residual stream at a specific layer, but only for the positions corresponding to a block of tokens rather than all tokens at once. This forces the model to re-learn representations in a localized fashion, improving the model's ability to capture local dependencies in the text.
backlog.title: Sliding Feature Injection

backlog.spec: Apply a sparse Adam where the optimizer only updates a fraction of the parameters each step, determined by a hard threshold on the residual of the weight. This introduces a regularization term that pruning the redundant features and forces the model to rely on the most salient features, similar to a dynamic sparse coding scheme.
backlog.title: Elastic-Weight Pruned Adam
